notes: Cats: the Régionale bank has one category for all of Italy, Italy (61 stems, 8 of them Piedmont, 10 on the national law and general geography every Italian subject shares), and the Village bank puts Piedmont in Italy North (62 stems, 20 of them Piedmont); no smaller door exists in either bank. Chapters: the Régionale chapter piedmont and the Village chapter Italy North, whose facts 1 to 3 are Piedmont. Region: the piedmont article, whose places hold Barolo's communes and crus, Barbaresco's three villages and crus, Roero, Asti, Acqui, Gavi, Alto Piemonte and Alta Langa, and whose producers hold eight of the Court's eleven names. Country: italy for the DOC, DOCG and IGT ladder and the label terms. Grapes: the Court's varieties that carry a profile, Muscat Blanc for Moscato Bianco, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir for the Alta Langa cell; Arneis and Brachetto have none. Techniques: oak for the large botti against barrique, extraction for the long traditional maceration, ageing terms for Riserva, tank method for Asti, Moscato d'Asti and Brachetto d'Acqui, traditional method for Alta Langa. Service tables: decanting (the young Barolo row), glassware (the Burgundy bowl names Nebbiolo) and temperatures (Barolo among the full tannic reds), the Court's service and ageing cells.
